tools.name: ChunkHound

tools.notes: Reference only, after a launch check that did not pass: this is a recording boundary, not a judgement on the project, which is current, MIT-licensed and documented. Upstream documents `chunkhound mcp [path]` as the stdio server, but the server never answered an MCP `initialize` request inside a fresh project within a 300-second window on this host. It failed in two different ways: left to itself uvx resolved Python 3.10, whose scipy build does not load on arm64 macOS, so the process died before accepting a connection; with Python 3.12 pinned it started but then stalled for minutes on an outbound HTTPS request with idle CPU, with and without `--no-daemon` and `--no-embeddings`, so `tools/list` was never reached. `--read-only` avoids that startup path and fails fast instead, because it needs an index that a fresh project does not have. Indexing is a separate explicit step (`chunkhound index .`), the database is created inside the project at `.chunkhound/db`, and semantic search or deep research also needs an embedding or LLM provider and credentials. Nothing here configures the tool, indexes a repository, or calls one of its tools.

The CLI and MCP server are Apache-2.0 and need no account or API key for local analysis; upstream's paid layers (PR Replay reports and a planned Roam Cloud) are not used by this recipe, and its README states that ordinary local analysis does not upload source code, indexes, findings or telemetry. No tool was called when the check ran, so index quality, language coverage and answer correctness are unverified.

tools.name: orm-lens

install.runtime: uv/uvx; Python 3.12 pinned for the launcher (the `mcp` extra requires >=3.10)

tools.notes: Pins the published PyPI release 1.16.0 (renamed from django-orm-lens; the old name still resolves to the same distribution). tools.name: Hippo
tools.description: Local-first long-term memory server for coding agents that stores project or global memories over MCP, strengthens them on recall and lets mistakes decay.

install.runtime: npx (Node.js 22.16 or newer, which the package declares in engines); the memory store is local - `~/.hippo` globally, or `.hippo/` in a project after `hippo init`

tools.notes: Pins the published npm release 3.2.2 in the form upstream documents for a client that does not want a global install (`"command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "hippo-memory", "mcp"]`); its README shows the same server as `hippo mcp` and `claude mcp add hippo-memory -- hippo mcp` for Claude Code. The design claim is outcome learning rather than storage with search: memories are strengthened each time they are recalled, a memory marked wrong drops out of the top results, and stale ones decay; the same server is documented for Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and OpenClaw, and data stays local. It overlaps `codebase-memory-mcp` and `headroom` in name only - this stores what an agent learned across sessions rather than a code index or compressed tool output. Upstream publishes its evals including failures and a retracted magnitude, and records that on Z0 round 2 over 16 repositories the repeat-mistake drop was not shown (-8.9 points, under the pre-registered 15-point minimum) while teach and correction turns cost about 12% less. Smoke-checked on macOS: the pinned command completed MCP initialize (server hippo-memory, reported version 3.2.2, protocol 2024-11-05) and listed 13 tools including hippo_recall, hippo_remember, hippo_outcome, hippo_conflicts and hippo_status.
